subject: Cross-border activation window & warm-failback agreement

Subject: Cross-border activation window & warm-failback agreement

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We need to lock an activation window for the Private deployment (EU primary, APAC warm-standby) so our legal and ops teams can sign off — particularly the failback guarantee and proof of residency during switchover.

High-level asks from our side: 
- A proposed 4-hour activation window per cutover (preferred UTC 02:00-06:00) with stepwise escalation triggers.
- Warm-failback description: how traffic will be redirected back to EU within X minutes and what data copies (if any) will cross boundaries during that window.
- Evidence types we can expect to provide to auditors (audit logs, KMS access records, networking flow captures).

I've attached our activation request form (finserve_activation_request.pdf). Can you confirm maintenance window availability in April and whether Redwood can provide the KMS handover matrix?

Appreciate a call if helpful — cc'ing Kenji from our Tokyo office who will be the EM for the cutover.

Best,
Sophia Müller
Head of Cloud Security, FinServe EU

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Cross-border activation window & warm-failback agreement

Sophia — thanks, good list. Drafting the operational agreement below and attaching our network runbook (redwood_network_runbook_v2.pdf) and preliminary KMS handover matrix.

Proposed activation + failback (summary):
1) Activation window: UTC 02:00-06:00 (EU local: 03:00-07:00 CET) — target cutover start time 02:30 UTC.
2) Traffic switch model: staged DNS + TCP proxy routing. Primary routing moves to APAC warm-standby only after health-checks and KV-cache priming complete.
3) Data residency during window: no new persistent customer data is written to APAC S3-equivalent storage. Short-lived KV cache replication allowed for latency-sensitive requests; caches are ephemeral and TTL-limited to 30 minutes.
4) Warm-failback procedure: if rollback required, route control-plane and session-token revocation occur first; data plane rollback (re-pointing storage mounts) completes within 45 minutes target. Expected total time-to-failback: 60 minutes in clean rollback.
5) Audit evidence: we can provide per-request residency headers, KMS key access logs for relevant encryption operations, and packet capture summaries for peering sessions (redacted to remove unrelated customer traffic).

Action items / owners: 
- Redwood (Vivek/Karthik): provide formal KMS handover matrix and sample residency log extract by 2027-03-25.
- FinServe (Sophia/Kenji): confirm preferred hard cutover date window in April and provide regulator contact for pre-notification.
- Redwood (Marissa): ops runbook dry-run and failback simulation — schedule proposed 2027-03-30.

Notes/constraints: 
- During activation we will use policy-based routing so we avoid any persistent object store writes in APAC (this keeps residency guarantees intact).
- Certain dependent third-party telemetry (CDN edge logs) may cross region for processing; we will provide configurable opt-outs.

If this looks OK I will put together a one-page activation SLA and a DocuSign envelope for signatures.

– Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwood.ai
(attachment: redwood_network_runbook_v2.pdf, pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 18:03:00 +0530
Subject: Re: Cross-border activation window & warm-failback agreement

Vivek / team — quick technical points from the runbook review: 

1) Network peering: we'll establish two BGP sessions per region (primary and failover) with explicit route-preference tags. During activation we will withdraw EU routes only after APAC health passes to prevent asymmetric routing.

2) KV priming: we'll run an incremental prefix prime to the APAC nodes for the top 1% of keys (measured by RPM) rather than full KV copy — reduces cross-border writes. Document will show sample key list (see runbook appendix).

3) KMS: for the KMS handover matrix, note that we will NOT export customer master keys; instead we will provide wrapped key transfer proofs (envelope encryption) and per-operation KMS logs scoped to the activation timeframe. TrustAssure has agreed to attest to the log integrity (see below).

4) Evidence checklist for auditors: per-request header (X-Redwood-Residency: eu-primary / apac-warm), KMS operation id ranges, and signed log blobs from the control plane. We should produce a small sample set and a redaction guide.

Minor ask: can Redwood legal confirm we can commit to the 60-minute failback SLA in the draft? If not, suggest we frame as a targeted SLO with exceptions for unexpected network partitions.
